explanations: The defect is in readFrom: this.queue.put(ping) is not awaited. put() correctly waits while the queue is full, but because the reader never waits on it, the for-await loop keeps pulling pings from the stream at full speed. Each blocked put() leaves a pending promise and a closure holding the ping in waitingPutters, so when the geo index slows down, memory grows without bound and the stream is never slowed. The fix is to await this.queue.put(ping) (inside a try/catch) so the reader stops pulling when the queue is full.

put() checks waitingTakers.shift() after the capacity loop; if a taker exists it is called with the item and put returns, so items is never touched. Nothing is pushed to items, the queue is not full so put does not wait, and the taker receives the actual item, not undefined.

dedupeLatest keeps one ping per driverId and replaces it only when prev.recordedAt < p.recordedAt, so the newest timestamp (300) wins regardless of arrival order. It never sends duplicates, and it does not prefer the last-arrived or the first ping.

The try/catch around upsertMany only logs a warning; the batch is not re-queued, and the while loop moves on to the next take(). For location pings this is a deliberate tradeoff since a newer ping will soon replace them. Nothing re-enqueues, and the catch prevents the error from ending the loop or rejecting runWriter.
